entries.reason: iOS 6 has no Network at all, so there is no connection to stop and nothing to answer; the call closes the socket this port opened and stops the path monitor it started, and asks twice is the same as asking once
entries.effect: the socket is closed and no handler is called after it

entries.reason: iOS 6 has no Network, so a connection is the port's own object holding the endpoint, the parameters and, once it is started, a real socket

entries.reason: the path a connection is on is the path the release's own reachability reports, which is what NWPathMonitor here already carries
entries.effect: the block is called on the connection's queue with the path when the connection starts and whenever the path changes; NULL removes it

entries.reason: a queue is a GCD queue, which iOS 6 has
entries.effect: the queue every handler of this connection is called on; a connection started without one does nothing, as the header says

entries.reason: viability is a real answer here, not a stand-in: the connection's own socket was connected, and a datagram connect fails exactly when the kernel has no route to the address
entries.effect: the block is called on the connection's queue with true when the socket is connected and the path is satisfied, with false when either stops being so, and again on every change; NULL removes it
entries.source: the SDK 16.4 header of Network (connection.h), and the port's own use of it in the Matter framework's device browser (src/darwin/Framework/CHIP/MTRDeviceConnectivityMonitor.mm at connectedhomeip v1.6.1.0)

entries.reason: starting is real work here: the host is resolved with getaddrinfo, a datagram socket is opened and connected, and the path monitor is started so the handlers have something to report
entries.effect: the socket is open and connected when the kernel has a route, and the handlers are called from then on; a second start is not a new attempt
entries.source: the SDK 16.4 header of Network (connection.h), and the port's own use of it in the Matter framework's device browser (src/darwin/Framework/CHIP/MTRDeviceConnectivityMonitor.mm at connectedhomeip v1.6.1.0)

entries.reason: an endpoint of a host and a port is exactly what the resolver takes, and iOS 6 has a resolver

entries.reason: the host is kept as it was given, and the string lives as long as the endpoint does

entries.reason: the port is kept as it was given, and the header answers it in host byte order as a number, with 0 for an endpoint that is not a host or address endpoint or has no port

entries.reason: an endpoint made by nw_endpoint_create_host is a host endpoint, and one that is not is not valid

entries.reason: the parameters carry what the connection has to open, which here is a datagram socket; each of the caller's two configure blocks is run exactly once, DTLS first, and the SDK's two sentinels are the empty blocks below so a caller that passes either gets the empty block run
entries.effect: parameters for a datagram connection, with each of the caller's configure blocks run exactly once
